facts.statement: Caryonosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous in southeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Caryonosuchus is an extinct genus of sphagesaurid notosuchian known from the Late Cretaceous of São Paulo State, southeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Caryonosuchus is a nearly complete front part of the skull and lower jaw.
facts.quote: Caryonosuchus is known only from the holotype specimen DGM 1411-R, a nearly complete anterior portion of the skull and lower jaw

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered near the city of Presidente Prudente in southwest São Paulo State.
facts.quote: It was found near Presidente Prudente City of southwest São Paulo State.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from the Adamantina Formation within the Bauru Basin, dating to the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Adamantina Formation of the Bauru Basin, which dates to the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Before its formal description, the fossil was tentatively assigned to the genus Sphagesaurus by Kellner and Campos in 1999.
facts.quote: DGM 1411-R was briefly mentioned before the description of Caryonosuchus. For example, Kellner & Campos (1999) tentatively assigned it to Sphagesaurus sp.

facts.statement: Researchers determined that the fossil represented a new genus and species rather than Sphagesaurus.
facts.quote: Thus, DGM 1411-R is regarded as a new genus and species.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2011 by Kellner, Campos, Riff, and de Andrade.
facts.quote: Caryonosuchus was first named by Alexander W. A. Kellner, Diogenes A. Campos, Douglas Riff and Marco Brandalise de Andrade in 2011

facts.statement: The species name honors Llewellyn Ivor Price, who originally described the holotype in an unpublished manuscript.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Llewellyn Ivor Price, a palaeontologist who described and named the genus Sphagesaurus and described the holotype of Caryonosuchus in an unpublished manuscript.

facts.statement: The snout features unique horn-like bumps on the upper jaw bones.
facts.quote: Caryonosuchus is characterized by a unique combination of characters, including three autapomorphies (unique characteristics) such as a rostrum with horn-like tubercles on the maxilla and on the premaxilla.

facts.statement: The snout displays unique rough ornamentation consisting of grooves and bony ridges.
facts.quote: Caryonosuchus also has autapomorphic rough ornamentation with grooves and bony ridges on its rostrum.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis classifies Caryonosuchus as an advanced member of the sphagesaurid family.
facts.quote: DGM 1411-R was found to be an advanced sphagesaurid in a phylogenetic analysis published by de Andrade et al. (2011).

facts.statement: Caryonosuchus belongs to the subfamily Sphagesaurinae.
Caryonosuchus is classified within the family Sphagesauridae.
Caryonosuchus lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
